visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with an introductory screen featuring five circular close-up inset images of different skin conditions: freckles, sun spots, liver spots, red acne marks, and black acne marks. These circles are arranged over a blurred background image of a woman's face, with a prominent clinic logo at the top and a tagline stating that not all pigmentation is the same. (2) The scene transitions to a detailed look at freckles. On the left side of the frame, there is a square close-up image showing light brown spots on a person's cheek and nose area. On the right side, several text bullet points appear against a clean white background, providing technical information about where they appear and their seasonal variability. (3) The next phase focuses on sun spots. A high-resolution photo showing larger, darker brown patches on the skin is positioned on the left. The right side is populated with text describing the causes related to ultraviolet rays and identifying common body areas like the face and neck where these spots typically manifest. (4) A detail slide for liver spots appears, featuring a close-up of skin with irregular, grayish-brown patches. Text to the right explains the hormonal and aging factors involved, noting that they are common in women and can be difficult to treat without consistent care, appearing prominently on the cheekbones. (5) The focus shifts to red acne marks. The visual evidence is a close-up photo of vibrant reddish-purple marks and inflammation on the skin. The accompanying text explains that these are formed by micro-vascular expansion during acne flare-ups and are common in people with cystic acne. (6) A slide for black acne marks is shown, displaying dark brown or grayish spots left behind after acne has healed. The text details how inflammatory responses lead to melanin deposition and mentions that topical treatments like acid-based products can help fade these specific marks. (7) The final phase is a white contact card screen. It displays the clinic branding again at the top. Below, there are stylized buttons and icons for LINE, a telephone number, and two location pins with addresses in New Taipei City and Taipei City, inviting viewers to contact them.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: 美上美皮膚科診所 DRX DERMATOLOGY CLINIC. [Slogan]: 不是所有的色素沈澱都是一樣的。. [Variety]: 雀斑. 曬斑. 肝斑. 紅痘疤. 黑痘疤. (2) [Variety]: 雀斑. [Subtitle]: 出現在暴露於陽光區域 (臉, 肩, 手臂). 在皮膚白的人更為突出. 冬天曝曬較少時會變淡一些. 預防及治療：每天擦防曬 (即便在陰天), 皮秒+紅寶石雷射可去除, 提高濃度A酸A醇+美白成分可淡化. (3) [Variety]: 曬斑. [Subtitle]: 因紫外線造成的扁平棕褐色或黑斑, 冬天不褪色, 與雀斑不同. 隨著年齡的增長慢慢出現. 最常見在臉部, 頸部, 肩部, 手部. 經常暴露在太陽底下, 防曬沒做足. 預防及治療：每天擦防曬 (即便在陰天), 每天使用A醇, 維他命C, 菸鹼醯胺B3, 光解酶, 皮秒+紅寶石或是高濃度煥膚療程有助於淡化. (4) [Variety]: 肝斑. [Subtitle]: 荷爾蒙變化, 老化, 長年日曬, 膠原蛋白流失. 在真皮層中的黑色素斑點, 形狀不規則, 若隱若現. 出現在額頭, 臉頰. 最常見於女性. 非常難治療, 沒做好保養會立即復發. 預防及治療：不要用對苯二酚+A酸藥物養膚治療, 長期使用維他命C, 菸鹼醯胺B3, 熊果素, 低濃度A醇. (5) [Variety]: 紅痘疤. [Subtitle]: 紅痘印是從痘痘發炎時形成的微血管擴張增生而來. 多發生於長囊腫型青春痘的人. 通常是由痘痘抓破或擠痘引起. 痘痘發炎太久大多會形成的紅痘印. 預防及治療：降低痘疤發炎, 儘快治療痘痘. 染料雷射, BBL, 585, UP雷射, 微針電波. (6) [Variety]: 黑痘疤. [Subtitle]: 痘痘發炎或癒合所產生的色素沈澱. 痘痘發炎程度較嚴重, 也會因色素沈澱而產生深色痘疤. 呈現棕色或深棕色. 常會因為痘痘癒合而導致色素沈澱濺濕. 是痘疤種類最快可以消除與治療的痘疤種類. 預防及治療：不要擠痘痘. 擦A酸, 杜鵑花酸, 美白成分的保養品可淡化. 打皮秒雷射可更加速消除痘印. (7) [Logo]: 美上美皮膚科診所 DRX DERMATOLOGY CLINIC. [Slogan]: LINE @drx.derm. 02-8985-9060. 新北市三重區正義北路104號2F. 台北市中山區南京東路一段96號. 歡迎聯繫我們 contact us.
